# LCC-C Wireless Power Transfer: Complete Simulation Results

This document was generated from the saved MATLAB/Simulink experiment data. It includes every recorded parameter-search evaluation, every saved frequency and load sweep point, the physical validation, and sensitivity results.

Source limitation: `technical bg.pdf` and the handwritten reference image were unavailable in the supplied project folder. The implemented topology follows the written task specification. No values from the handwritten answer were used as optimizer inputs.

**Software:** MATLAB R2026b Update 1; Simulink 26.2; Simscape Electrical 26.2; Optimization Toolbox 26.2.  
**Data:** [results.csv](results.csv), [design_results.mat](design_results.mat), [validation_results.mat](validation_results.mat), [simulation_log.txt](simulation_log.txt).

## 1. Circuit, fixed inputs, and assumptions

Topology: 1 V rms AC source -> series compensation inductor L -> shunt capacitor C -> series capacitor C1 -> transmitter winding resistance R1 and coil L1. The magnetically coupled receiver coil L2 drives its own series winding resistance R2, series capacitor C2, and resistive load R. The two windings are electrically separate. The mutual-inductor block has no additional winding resistance.

| Fixed quantity | Value |
|---|---:|
| Operating frequency | 13.560000 MHz |
| Target/load resistance | 12.500000 ohm |
| Transmitter self-inductance L1 | 486.020000 nH |
| Receiver self-inductance L2 | 486.020000 nH |
| Unloaded Q1 | 951.100000 |
| Unloaded Q2 | 931.000000 |
| R1 = 2 pi f L1 / Q1 | 0.043537904 ohm |
| R2 = 2 pi f L2 / Q2 | 0.044477874 ohm |

Compensation components are ideal in this first design: no inductor/capacitor ESR, dielectric loss, core loss, switching loss, rectifier loss, radiation loss, or frequency-dependent winding resistance is included. These omissions limit the efficiency prediction.

## 2. Experiment A: coupling from simulated optimum-load matching

The frequency-domain Simulink model evaluated input power, load power, and coil-to-coil efficiency for 12 candidate k values and 45 load values per candidate. Coil-to-coil efficiency is load power divided by real power entering the primary coil branch. A numerical load optimization and root search then solved R_opt(k) = 12.5 ohm. The search did not maximize efficiency over k.

| Matched result | Value |
|---|---:|
| Simulated optimum load R_opt | 12.499999997 ohm |
| Coupling coefficient k | 0.2986590621 |
| Inferred mutual inductance M | 145.154277361 nH |
| Coil-to-coil efficiency at design | 0.99290878 (99.29088%) |

M is an inferred design target under the stated coil model. It is not a measurement of an existing coil pair.

## 3. Experiment B: simulation-driven L and C inverse design

At each candidate L and C, Simulink evaluated the complete coupled-network phasors and complex input impedance. C2 was tuned to cancel L2 at 13.56 MHz. For each L, C1 was set by the LCC series-compensation constraint C1 = 1/[omega^2(L1-L)]. The objective penalized error in real Zin, imaginary Zin, and omega^2 L C - 1. Three independent starting points were refined with Nelder-Mead.

## 4. Independent physical Simscape validation

The physical model used the ode23t solver with a maximum step of T/25. The transient was extended from 20 to 40 microseconds because the first comparison did not meet the 0.1% criterion. The final measurement compared adjacent 20-cycle phasor windows; their largest relative change was below 0.1%.

| Physical measurement | Value |
|---|---:|
| Stop time | 40.000 microseconds |
| Window change | 0.000179278943 |
| Input voltage | 0.999973341 V rms |
| Input current | 0.033341007 A rms |

## 6. Frequency, load, and component sensitivity

The frequency sweep contains 81 Simulink evaluations from 10.848 to 16.272 MHz. The load sweep contains 41 evaluations from 6 to 25 ohm. The complete numeric values appear in Appendices A and B below. With ideal LCC compensation, simulated transmitter coil current was effectively load independent within numerical precision.

| Sensitivity summary | Value |
|---|---:|
| Maximum relative Tx current change across load sweep | 3.9883133e-16 |

## Reproduction and saved files

The physical model `LCCC_inverse_design.slx` and the phasor evaluator `LCCC_phasor.slx` were reopened and compiled after the full experiment. The scripts `build_model.m`, `optimise_parameters.m`, `validate_design.m`, `phasor_network.m`, and `lccc_evaluate.m` implement the workflow; `write_full_reports.m` generates these two Markdown documents from saved data. The MATLAB execution diary is `simulation_log.txt`. Running the command below rebuilds the models and overwrites the generated result files.

```powershell
& 'C:\Program Files\MATLAB\R2026b\bin\matlab.exe' -batch "cd('C:\Users\charl\Documents\LCCC_inverse_design'); run_experiment"
```
